title: Classic Diner Breakfast
subtitle: eggs your way, crispy bacon, golden home fries and buttered toast
imageAlt: Two fried eggs, crispy bacon strips, golden home fries and buttered toast on a cream plate with a navy napkin

beforeYouStart.text: Bacon goes in the oven so the stove is free for potatoes and eggs.
Par-cook the potatoes in the microwave so the home fries crisp in 12 minutes.

steps.title: Bacon
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Lay the bacon on a foil-lined baking sheet and bake 15–18 minutes, until crisp. Drain on paper towel.

steps.title: Par-cook
steps.text: Meanwhile, microwave the potatoes in a covered bowl with 2 tbsp water for 5 minutes, until just tender. Drain.

steps.title: Home fries
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add the potatoes in one layer and cook 10–12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until golden. Add the onion, paprika, salt and pepper for the last 5 minutes. Keep warm in the oven, turned off.

steps.title: Eggs
steps.text: Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low. Crack in the eggs, sprinkle with salt, cover and cook 3–4 minutes, until the whites are completely set and the yolks are firm. Flip for over-easy if you like, 30 seconds.

steps.title: Toast and serve
steps.text: Toast and butter the bread. Plate the eggs, bacon, home fries and toast.

fixIt.fix: Start it in a cold oven next time, or use thicker slices.
Lower the heat; covering the pan sets the tops gently.
Dry the potatoes well and don't crowd the pan.

saleTip: No Frills bacon is often 2 for $10; freeze one pack flat.
swap: Peameal bacon slices for bacon (cook to 71°C / 160°F). Rye or whole wheat toast.
leftovers: Leftover home fries and bacon go into breakfast burritos.
doneness: Fried eggs until the whites and yolks are firm, the Health Canada advice for eggs; bacon cooked crisp.
source: Based on classic Canadian diner breakfasts and tested oven-bacon and home fry methods (Canadian Living, Serious Eats).
prepAhead: Cube the potatoes the night before and keep them covered in cold water in the fridge.
reheat: Home fries and bacon in a skillet over medium 3–4 minutes, until 74°C (165°F). Cook eggs fresh.

basic.note: Eggs, bacon and toast; no home fries.

fancy.note: Add warm baked beans and pan-fried tomato halves, a full Sunday plate.

addSteps.title: Beans and tomatoes
addSteps.text: Warm the beans in a small pot until bubbling. Sear the tomato halves cut side down in the bacon pan drippings 2 minutes.

plating: Eggs at the centre, bacon crossed beside.

why.1-2: Covering the pan steams the tops so the yolks firm up without crisping the whites.
why.0-0: Yukon Golds crisp outside and stay creamy inside.

funFact: The 'diner' gets its name from railway dining cars; many early diners were built in factories and shipped on trucks.

keeps.note: eggs and toast are best fresh; keep leftover home fries and bacon in the fridge

drink: Bottomless coffee, or orange juice with a splash of soda water.
